xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:AnyOtherInformationForDisclosu: The Company (Appellant) assessed by the Income Tax Officer, National Faceless Assessment Centre, Delhi, filed its original and revised income tax returns for AY 2018-19, declaring an income of Rs.2,27,61,310. The case was selected for limited scrutiny due to large agricultural income reported under business ITR. During assessment under Section 143(3) r.w.s. 144B of the Income Tax Act, dated 23.06.2021, the Assessing Officer (AO) added Rs.69,54,713 to the income and initiated penalty proceedings under Section 271AAC. The AO alleged that this amount was unexplained cash credit under Section 68, on account of failure of appellant to substantiate its agricultural income claim resulting due to inability to provide supporting documents demanded during a COVID-19 pandemic lockdown. Despite requesting an adjournment, the AO proceeded with the assessment and disregarded the explanations provided. The total assessed income was revised to a greater value. The company is of the view that the order passed is neither factually nor legally tenable, and the imposition of penalty is unjustified.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Income Tax Officer, National Assessent Centre, Delhi
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: The Company has filed an appeal on 1st September 2021 before the Joint Commissioner (Appeals) / Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeals) against the assessment order and demand notice issued by the Income Tax Officer, National Faceless Assessment Centre, Delhi, dated 23rd June 2021, under Section 143(3) read with Section 144B of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The appeal is currently under review, and the Company is awaiting further directions or a final decision from the appellate authority.
